verdicts.what_would_bite: The adjudication's stated mechanism is true — pass_scope (Passes.jl:261-267) sets the act range's `from` to the last GRADED pass's head, pass_open hands the act verifier only `range => fixrange` (:450), verify-act.js:74 defines UNDONE as "nothing in the diff addresses this finding", and grade discards the prior act verdict for any in-scope id (:551-555, :611), so honored closure is unreachable; ARCHITECTURE §11 (L2129-2139) records exactly this and measures it: "22 of 40 ids closed this way". What the dismissal never accounts for is the cost of the channel it used. `Ledger` entry ⇒ `Preflight.adjudicated_titles` (Preflight.jl:480) ⇒ (a) the SEARCHING panel of every future check-consistency round of this package via render_args (Preflight.jl:516) → panel.js:56 "Do NOT spend a finding on anything they cover"; (b) the blind verifier via pass_open's `base` (Passes.jl:415) → verify-state.js:45-46 "one of them is verdict NOT-A-DEFECT with 'owner-adjudicated' as evidence"; (c) verify-act.js:52 "the owner has ruled these findings NOT to be defects (they were deliberately left alone)". All three promise "Nothing merely FIXED is listed" — an invariant this closure breaks, since bank()'s DEAD-or-REJECTED docstring WAS a real defect (old text "Any DEAD lane ⇒ exit 2 and nothing frozen") and WAS fixed (Rounds.jl:439-443). The entry is permanent: adjudicated_titles filters neither by round/date nor by `expires` (contrast Ledger.entries, Ledger.jl:61), and nothing removes it when the deferred remedy ships and the id regrades HONORED. So a later regression of that docstring is pre-suppressed for a defect no owner ever ruled on — silently, for this id and the other 21 closed the same way. grade also counts it (`adjudicated += 1`), inflating `adjudicated_share`, which Fleet.jl:133 prints as a cross-round comparable rate.
